chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Ibn Fazzal, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Abu al-Yaqthan, from Yaqub ibn al-Dahhak, from a man from our companions, Sirraj, who was a servant of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent me regarding a need, and he was at Al-Hira, I and a group of his slaves. So we went regarding it, then we returned gloomy.

He said: And my bed was in the Ha'ir (enclosure) where we were lodging. So I came while I was in that state, and I threw myself (down). So while I was like that, behold, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) had come over.

He said: So he said, 'We have come to you,' or he said, 'I have come to you.' So I sat up straight, and he sat upon the middle of my bed. So he asked me about what he had sent me for, so I informed him. So he praised Allah.
Then there flowed a mention of a group of people, so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We disavow from them. They are not saying what we are saying.'
He said: So he said, 'If they were befriending us and not saying what you are saying, would you be disassociating from them?'
He said: I said, 'Yes.'
He said: 'So since that which is with us is not what is with you, so it would be befitting for us to disassociate from you?'
He said: I said, 'No, may I be sacrificed for you!'
He said: 'And since that which is with Allah is what is not with us, so what is your view, should we drop it?'
I said, 'No, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you! What should we do?'

He said: 'So befriend them and do not disassociate from them. From the Muslims, there is the one for whom there is one portion, and from them is the one for whom there are two portions, and from them is the one for whom there are three portions, and from them is the one for whom there are four portions, and from them is the one for whom there are five portions, and from them is the one for whom there are six portions, and from them is the one for whom there are seven portions.'

So it is not befitting that the owner of the one portion be burdened with what is upon the owner of the two portions, nor the owner of the two portions with what is upon the owner of the three, nor the owner of the three with what is upon the owner of the four, nor the owner of the four with what is upon the owner of the five, nor the owner of the five with what is upon the owner of the six, nor the owner of the six with what is upon the owner of the seven.

And I shall strike an example for you. A man had a neighbor, and he was a Christian. So he invited him to Islam and adorned it for him. So he responded to it. So he went over at pre-dawn and knocked the door upon him.
So he said to him, 'Who is this?' He said, 'I am so and so.' He said, 'And what is your need?' So he said, 'You should perform ablution and wear your clothes and come with me to the Salat.'
So he performed ablution and wore his clothes and went with him.
So they both prayed whatever Allah so Desired, then prayed the Fajr Salat. Then they both remained until the morning.

So he arose, the one who used to be a Christian, intending to go to his house. So the man said to him, 'Where are you going? The day is short, and that which is between you and the Dhuhr Salat is little (time).'
So he sat with him until he prayed the Dhuhr Salat. Then he said, 'And how little (time) is between the Dhuhr and the Asr Salat.' So he withheld him until he prayed the Asr.
Then he arose and intended to leave to go to his house. So he said to him, 'This is the end of the day, and it is less than its beginning.' So he withheld him until he prayed the Maghrib.
Then he intended to leave to go to his house, so he said to him, 'But rather, there remains one Salat (only).' So he remained until he had prayed the Isha the last. Then they both dispersed.
So when it was the next pre-dawn upon him, he knocked the door upon him. So he said, 'Who is this?' He said, 'I am so and so.' He said, 'And what is your need?'
He said, 'Perform ablution and wear your clothes, and come out with me, so pray.'
He said, 'Seek for this religion the one who is more free (for time) than I am, and I am a poor person, and upon me are dependants.'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He entered him into something (but then he) took it out from him', or he said: 'He entered him from the likes of those ones and took him out from the likes of this.'
ai.seo_question: How should Shia Muslims relate to those who have different levels of faith and practice?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the principle of *Tawalli* (affiliation) and *Tabarri* (disassociation) by distinguishing between varying degrees of faith (*as-hab al-as-ham*), advising believers not to judge or disassociate from those with lesser practice. The Imam uses the parable of a newly converted neighbor to illustrate that spiritual maturity is a gradual process, and one should accommodate others according to their current capacity rather than imposing the strict standards of the most devout. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on nuanced social engagement, where maintaining community bonds takes precedence over rigid exclusivity for those still on their spiritual journey.

en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa all from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm from abu al-Yaqzan from Ya’qub ibn al-Dahhak from a man of our people, Sarraj who was a servant of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) once sent me with a group of his followers for an errand and at that time he was in Hirah (a place near Kufa, Iraq). We left for it and returned depressed.

My bed was in al-Ha’ir (a comfortable private quarter). I went there in an upset condition and threw myself thereat. At this time abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) came in saying, ‘We have come to see you,’ or he said, ‘We have come to you.’
I then sat up straight and he sat in the middle of my bed and asked me about the errand for which he had sent me. I reported to him and he thanked Allah.
Thereafter, a mention of certain people came up and I said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, we disassociate from these people; they do not say what we say.’
The Imam then said, ‘If they love and support us, but do not say what you say, do you (still) disassociate from them?’
I then said, ‘Yes, we do so.’
“The Imam said, ‘It is just like this (’ A’immah’s case). We have what you do not have. Should we disassociate from you?’
I then said, ‘No, may Allah keep my soul in service for your cause.’
The Imam said, ‘It is just like this (the case of Allah). With Him there is what we do not have. Do you think we should give it up?’
“I then said, ‘No, may Allah keep my soul in service for your cause. We should not do so.’

The Imam said, ‘Be friends with them and do not disassociate from them. Among the Muslims there are those who have only one share, those who have two shares, three shares, four shares, five shares, six shares and those who have seven shares.

It is not proper for those who have one share to blame those who have two shares, or those who have two shares to blame those who have three shares, those who have three shares to blame those who have four shares, those who have four shares to blame those who have five shares, those who have five shares to blame those who have six shares and those who have six shares to blame those who have seven shares.
I will give an example: “A man had a Christian neighbor to whom he preached Islam attractively and the neighbor accepted. It was early next morning when he knocked at his (convert’s) door.
He said, ‘Who is it?’ He (the preacher) said, ‘I am so and so.’ ‘What do you want?’ the (convert) said. ‘Make Wuzu, dress up in your two cloths and join us for prayer,’ said the preacher.
The new convert then made Wuzu, dressed up in his two pieces of cloth and joined him.
They performed prayers a great deal. Then they prayed the morning-prayer, then waited until it was light.
The convert got up to go home and the man asked him, ‘Where are you going? The day is short. The time left to noontime is very little.’

The new convert sat down with him until noontime and they prayed the noontime prayer. Then he said that there is very little time to afternoon prayer. He prevented the new convert from going home until they said the afternoon prayer.

He then wanted to go home but he (the preacher) said, ‘It is the last part of the day and is less than the beginning of it.’ So he (the preacher) stopped him until they performed the prayer at sunset.
Then the new convert wanted to go home, he (the preacher) said, ‘Only one more prayer is left.’ He then waited until they performed the late evening prayer and then they departed each other.

Next early morning he (the preacher) went and knocked at the door of the new convert. He (the new convert) asked, ‘Who is it?’ He (the preacher) said, ‘I am so and so.’ He (the new convert) asked, ‘What do you want?’
He (the preacher) said, ‘Make Wuzu, dress up in your two pieces of cloth and join us for prayer.’
He (the Christian man) said, ‘Find other persons for this religion who have more free time. I am a poor person with a family to feed.’

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then said, ‘He (the preacher) took him (Christian) into a thing in such a way that it took him (the new convert) out of it. Or that the Imam said, ‘Took him in like this and forced him out like that.’”
